posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
I read that the deal is not final and may not happen.  If it does, the consensus is that RPG maker will probably see no changes... but many are very worried.
Pros:  Sony is big and might provide a stable home.  It keeps pay for play vampires away from RPG maker.  It could gain a platform for sales or media.
Cons:  Sony could neglect RPGmaker or favor a change in it's direction.  It could force registrations of users or interfere with Itch.io/Steam as sales platforms.  Sony is so big, they might not respect the large community size that RPG maker has built and maintains.

posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
Kadokawa is big enough that it is likely to retain its internal structure, especially given how many companies they themselves own and manage. So, really, it will be a long while, if ever, that big changes to the trajectory of RPG Maker would occur.
My biggest concern would be that Sony eventually determines that, because of the failure of Unite and lack of spectacular success following, they might pull the plug on supporting this project in its entirety. That would bring the survival of this forum into question (Though I have no idea how this place operates, given the different companies involved in the different engines, historically)

posts.author: Tai_MT
posts.body:
Honestly, I'm more concerned about what Sony will do with the ANIME it will be acquiring the rights to.  Especially considering its stance on ecchi and adult themes in "anime-esque" games that grace its gaming platform (or no longer grace its platform, or can't be obtained on its platform now).
The two worst things I can imagine Sony dong to RPG Maker are this:
1.  Shutting down RPG Maker and no longer having any support for it so it dies off.
2.  Taking control of any/all UI elements involved.  If the Playstation menus and UI are anything to go on for how they view structuring anything...  the makers are going to become nightmarish to navigate.  The playstation menu/UI makes the Xbox one look sane in comparison.

posts.body: I was not aware Sony owned Crunchyroll.  Though, I do wonder how Sony would approach a studio that produces anime compared to one that merely streams it for a fee.  Especially when you consider what is in the catalogue of Kadokawa's anime...

posts.author: Timeline_man
posts.body:
Tai_MT said:
I was not aware Sony owned Crunchyroll.  Though, I do wonder how Sony would approach a studio that produces anime compared to one that merely streams it for a fee.  Especially when you consider what is in the catalogue of Kadokawa's anime...
Click to expand...
That seems like some vague fearmongering. A lot of the anime Kadokawa produce comes from the manga that they also publish, and they own a good few publishing companies.
Kadokawa is already massive, and they make a lot of money through their vast number of businesses already. Sony is ultimately in the business of making money. The properties Kadokawa own make money, which is ultimately what Sony wants out of this deal: for that money to be added to their own, also massive, amount of money. Slashing a considerable number of titles in distribution is counterproductive.
I understand that this comes from the censor-heavy handling of Playstation titles, but those are all games made with properties they didn't own. They didn't really care how those titles sold, they didn't own them.
